step_model.formula: seconds per large step = max(floor_s + (tiles - 1) x tile_s, cells x ns_per_cell_step x 1e-9), tiles = the closure tiles a step launches (1 for the whole domain)
step_model.why: a GM1 step is host-launch-bound on small grids (a flat floor of 1300-1400 launches per step) and scales with cells once the device work exceeds it; the per-cell cost stays flat as the storm grows
step_model.acoustic_substeps: not scaled: the 39.3 M-cell deck's body at 6 substeps ran 40.8-45.9 ns per cell-step on the RTX 3080 against 41.8 at 4, inside the band
step_model.tiles: every closure tile launches the closure's operations again, so a tiled grid whose tiles hold little device work is launch-bound: on the RTX 3080 160 x 160 x 80 at tile 128 ran 1.8 x its whole-domain speed (estimator verification)

morrison-mp10.label: measured
morrison-mp10.basis: measured on an RTX 3080 10 GB reference card: 0.2190 s per step, the mean over 200 steps at 256 x 256 x 80 (5.24 M cells), closure tile 128, 4 sound-wave steps per step; the whole-domain tile ran 0.2186 s
morrison-mp10.floor_basis: measured on an RTX 3080 10 GB reference card: the stock 1 km supercell's mean step time over 1200 steps, averaged over two runs (0.0429 and 0.0523 s)
morrison-mp10.tile_basis: the host seconds each closure tile after the first adds, measured on an RTX 3080 10 GB reference card: 0.036, 0.045 and 0.034 s at 160 x 160, 192 x 192 and 264 x 264 x 80 with tile 128, which ran 0.155, 0.184 and 0.321 s per step against 0.086, 0.123 and 0.233 s for their cells alone; 256 x 256 (4 full tiles) and 240 x 240 at 500 m stay device-bound

wsm6-mp6.floor_basis: measured on an RTX 3080 10 GB reference card: the stock 1 km supercell's mean WSM6 step time over 1200 steps, averaged over two runs (0.0433 and 0.0326 s)
wsm6-mp6.tile_basis: the Morrison runs' per-tile host cost: the closure tile launches the same operations under either scheme

memory_model.formula: device bytes = priced_peak + fixed_bytes + per_cell_bytes x cells + component_extra_bytes
memory_model.priced_peak: cartesian_door.closure_decomposition_peak_bytes at the run's own closure tile: the dynamics phase peak, the persistent closure and reflectivity residents, and the largest of the held, TKE and physics-block workspaces (host-side, CUDA-cold)
memory_model.fit_method: chosen over the seven Morrison runs then in hand (the four build runs and three estimator verification runs, 128 x 128 x 40, 128 x 128 x 80 and 192 x 192 x 80 on the RTX 3080): 0.55 GB + 80 B per cell puts every one within 7.7 % (the strict minimax, 0.53 GB + 99 B, gives 7.0 % but is 4.6 % high at 39.3 M cells); the WSM6 extra is the mean of the two RTX 3080 WSM6 rows' remainders, 0.56 GB. Four later verification runs (160 x 160, 192 x 192 whole-domain, 264 x 264 and 240 x 240 at 500 m) check it out of sample. The build fit (0.48 GB + 78 B) was 11 % low at 128 x 128 x 80, the direction that says fits and then runs out of memory

memory_model.replaces: an earlier fit, 1.2 GB + 461 B/cell, which is within 5 % at 1.3-39 M cells at tile 128 but 72 % high at the stock deck's 0.58 M cells (1.47 GB against 0.86 GB measured then)
memory_model.replaced: 0.48 GB + 78 B per cell + 0.65 GB for WSM6 (the build fit over four Morrison rows)

tile_rule.rule: a document that declares no closure tile runs one whole-domain tile (cartesian_door.resolve_closure_tiles); the estimator prices that, and recommends tile 128 when the whole domain does not fit the GPU's free memory, or when tile 128 needs less memory at no more than 3 % more estimated step time
tile_rule.why: on the RTX 3080 at 256 x 256 x 80 the two ran at the same speed (0.2190 against 0.2186 s/step) and tile 128 needed 1.5 GB less (3534 against 4992 MiB); the whole-domain tile's held workspace grows as 470 B/cell. Tile 128 is not free on grids that are not multiples of it: at 192 x 192 x 80 it ran 0.184 s/step against 0.116 for the whole domain (estimator verification)
tile_rule.exception: CM1's cecd=2/3 water-roughness iteration is the one path whose tiled words differ from untiled (docs/GM1-CARTESIAN-RUNTIME.md); with a surface layer over water the recommendation says so

startup.formula: seconds from launch to the first large step = fixed_s + per_cell_s x cells
startup.label: measured
startup.basis: least squares over eight runs from 0.58 M to 39.3 M cells (8.4 to 36.1 s); NVRTC compiles 60-80 programs in 6-8 s every run

io.label: measured
io.basis: measured: a frame's blocking snapshot runs at 1.1-1.9 GB/s and a restart in mid-run at 0.7 GB/s; the last frame and restart are waited for, 0.26-0.39 GB/s measured

disk.netcdf_basis: an earlier conversion of 5.24 M-cell frames: 0.44 GB raw against 0.57 GB of cm1out netCDF; the cm1out writer replaces this ratio with its own count
disk.quicklook_label: measured: six 1920 x 1080 PNGs and their 480 x 270 thumbnails, 2.68-3.05 MB per frame on CM1's stock 1 km run, the 250 m run and a 100 m frame (the quick-look measurement record)

host_locked.formula: history payload + restart payload (the two page-locked publication arenas)
host_locked.basis: every measured run's locked host buffers equal the plan's two payloads (572,271,168 + 1,469,366,832 bytes at 256 x 256 x 80)
